raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in ASGI middleware that strips Unicode tag characters (U+E0020 to U+E007F) from request bodies sent to the LLM generation endpoints, enabled with `VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE=true`. Supersedes #41762 (closed), which had an approval on the same design.

## Claims

- Tag characters are invisible to humans but are tokenized by the model and can steer or destabilize generations; with the flag set they are removed before the request reaches the handler, for both encodings a JSON client can use (raw UTF-8 and `\uDB40\uDCxx` escapes).
- Covers `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages` and `/cohere/v2/chat`; all other routes, methods and characters (including emoji) are untouched.
- Off by default; zero cost on clean payloads beyond two substring checks on the buffered body.
- Fixes a bug present in the earlier revisions of this PR: the replayed `receive()` reported a synthetic `http.disconnect`, which made `with_cancellation` cancel every filtered request (empty response) and would have truncated streaming responses.

## Validation

Unit tests (`tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_middleware.py`, 18 cases) run the middleware against a FastAPI echo app and include a regression test that uses the real `with_cancellation` decorator and a `StreamingResponse` test; both fail on the previous revision and pass now.

End-to-end tests (`tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_integration.py`) start `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --load-format dummy` with the flag set and check, via `usage.prompt_tokens`/`input_tokens` against the unfiltered `/tokenize` endpoint, that chat, completions (`echo=True`), streaming chat, Responses and Anthropic Messages requests all drop the tag characters. Both test files live under `tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/`, which the Entrypoints Integration CI step collects.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_middleware.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_integration.py -v
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
```

Results on an RTX 3500 Ada (12 GB), vLLM at the PR commit:

| Suite | Fixed middleware | Pre-fix middleware (same tests) |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (`test_unicode_filter_middleware.py`) | 18 passed | 6 failed (cancellation, streaming, escapes, pattern) |
| Real server (`test_unicode_filter_integration.py`) | 7 passed | 6 of 7 failed (empty bodies, no stream events, unfiltered token counts on Responses/Anthropic); control passed |
| `pre-commit run --files ...` | all hooks pass | n/a |

Server used by the integration test: `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --load-format dummy --max-model-len 512 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3` with `VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE=true`.

## Details

- Pure ASGI middleware (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/unicode_filter.py`), registered in `init_entrypoints_middleware` inside the authentication middleware so unauthenticated requests are rejected before any body is buffered.
- Filtering runs on the UTF-8 bytes: every codepoint in the block is a 4-byte sequence with prefix `F3 A0 80|81`, so one bytes regex covers the block without a decode/encode round trip. A second regex handles the JSON surrogate-pair escape and leaves escaped backslashes (`\\uDB40`) alone, since those are literal text.
- The body is buffered once in the middleware and replayed to the app; after the replay, `receive()` defers to the server's own `receive()` so disconnect detection keeps working.
- Limitation: only JSON-encoded tag characters in the request body are handled; characters that arrive through other channels (for example, a prompt fetched by the model from a tool result) are out of scope.
- The toggle is an environment variable, matching the predecessor PR's approved design; a `FrontendArgs` flag would also fit if maintainers prefer that.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the rebase, the bug fix, the tests and this description; every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the commands above were run locally on an RTX 3500 Ada (12 GB).

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces `UnicodeFilterMiddleware` to sanitize request payloads by stripping characters in the Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 to U+E007F) for the chat and completions endpoints. This optional feature, configurable via environment variables, aims to prevent unpredictable model responses caused by invisible tokens. The PR includes documentation and unit tests. Feedback was provided to optimize the middleware's path handling by using `scope['path']` directly.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `URL(scope=scope).path.removeprefix(root_path)` is inefficient as it involves creating a new `URL` object and performing string concatenation/parsing for every `POST` request. In ASGI, `scope["path"]` is already defined as the path relative to `root_path`. You can use it directly to achieve the same result much more efficiently.

```suggestion
        path = scope["path"]
```

@@ -86,6 +88,115 @@ def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> Awaitable[None
         return self.app(scope, receive, send)
 
 
+class UnicodeFilterMiddleware:
+    """
+    Pure ASGI middleware that sanitizes incoming request payloads by
+    stripping characters in the Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 to U+E007F)
+    from request bodies sent to LLM completion endpoints.
+
+    These characters are invisible to humans but are tokenized by language
+    models, which can lead to unpredictable responses. The middleware is
+    intended to clean up requests from clients that emit unwanted Unicode
+    content. Normal Unicode, including emojis, is left untouched. Only
+    POST requests whose path matches :attr:`ROUTES_TO_FILTER` are
+    inspected; all other traffic passes through unchanged.
+
+    Pass ``use_translation_table=True`` to filter via ``str.translate``
+    with a precomputed table, which can be faster than the regex on
+    large payloads.
+    """
+
+    ROUTES_TO_FILTER: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(
+        {"/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/completions"}
+    )
+
+    # Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 - U+E007F).
+    UNICODE_PATTERN: ClassVar[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"[\U000E0020-\U000E007F]")
+    _TRANSLATION_TABLE: ClassVar[dict[int, None]] = dict.fromkeys(
+        range(0xE0020, 0xE0080)
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, use_translation_table: bool = False) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+        self.use_translation_table = use_translation_table
+
+    def _filter_text(self, text: str) -> str:
+        if self.use_translation_table:
+            return text.translate(self._TRANSLATION_TABLE)
+        return self.UNICODE_PATTERN.sub("", text)
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http" or scope.get("method") != "POST":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        root_path = scope.get("root_path", "")
+        path = URL(scope=scope).path.removeprefix(root_path)

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces `UnicodeFilterMiddleware` to sanitize request payloads by stripping characters in the Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 to U+E007F) for the chat and completions endpoints. This optional feature, configurable via environment variables, aims to prevent unpredictable model responses caused by invisible tokens. The PR includes documentation and unit tests. Feedback was provided to optimize the middleware's path handling by using `scope['path']` directly.
